nodes.label: Laverta Logo Design Direction
nodes.description: A geometric sign with editorial lines converging on a marker should suggest a report moving to a source and a correction returning to people. The lowercase wordmark and monochrome symbol should stay legible at small sizes. The brief requests editable SVG variants and rejects imagery that implies automated truth judgments or invents an etymology.

nodes.label: Laverta Editorial and AI Safeguards
nodes.description: A journalist owns the verdict and correction. Sources must be consultable; finding a source or matching text does not by itself establish correctness or currency. Unreliable or absent sources do not justify an automatic verdict. Priority is a processing order, anonymization is reviewable, and report counts do not establish rumor prevalence.

nodes.label: Recommended Vertical Demo Slice
nodes.description: Demonstrate a complete web report, confirmed summary, LV tracking code, journalist queue, editable AI proposals, consultable sources, human verdict, shareable correction and tracking or publication page. External messaging, maps and alerts remain roadmap unless tested.
nodes.rationale: This small end-to-end slice demonstrates the return-to-public loop while clearly separating concepts and untested integrations from working capabilities.

nodes.label: Laverta Correction Return Loop
nodes.description: Laverta connects a reporter, journalist, organization that can respond, and local network that can relay a correction. A report gets an identifier, becomes a verifiable case, and may lead to a correction returned to reporters and voluntary relays.
nodes.rationale: The return loop is the distinctive promise to demonstrate; image analysis alone does not make that promise tangible.

nodes.label: Correction Circulation Lever
nodes.description: The PDF proposes returning corrections to reporters, AI-generated shareable French and Malagasy visuals, voluntary group and community relays, partner newsroom alerts, and a public verification database.

nodes.label: Journalist Retains the Verdict
nodes.description: The PDF says AI assists the journalist and the journalist makes the decision; it also states that no technology will eliminate disinformation entirely.

nodes.label: God's Eye View Privacy and Data-License Caveats
nodes.description: The analysis flags surveillance-style views and ALPR/CCTV layers as privacy risks and does not recommend them for the prototype. The code's MIT license does not automatically cover imagery or external feeds.
nodes.norm_label: god's eye view privacy and data-license caveats

nodes.label: Laverta Editorial Brand Direction
nodes.description: The brand presents a newsroom-oriented service for verified information in Madagascar. It shows the path from report to evidence to public return, keeps the newsroom as final decision-maker, makes uncertainty explicit, protects identities by default, and treats corrections as shareable objects.
nodes.rationale: The visual identity should make the circulation of information and the correction’s return to the people concerned visible.

nodes.label: God's Eye View Malagasy Translation Preview
nodes.description: The local mg preview translates 52 of 2,730 messages; missing strings fall back to English. It has not been reviewed by a native Malagasy speaker and must not be presented as a finished Malagasy interface.
nodes.norm_label: god's eye view malagasy translation preview

nodes.label: God's Eye View as a Complementary Geographic Check
nodes.community_name: IFM Video Need: Authenticate Images for Journalists
nodes.description: The analysis recommends keeping Laverta as the main image-and-claim verification workflow and using God's Eye View only as a proposed complementary map view for checking an alleged location. Each layer needs a source, date, coverage and limitations; the recommendation is not evidence of an implemented integration.
nodes.norm_label: god's eye view as a complementary geographic check
nodes.rationale: Geographic context can provide a clue for a journalist's verification, but cannot establish image authenticity, date or integrity.

nodes.label: God's Eye View Does Not Authenticate an Image
nodes.community_name: IFM Video Need: Authenticate Images for Journalists
nodes.description: The analysis says the tool does not collect a photo and claim, perform reverse-image search, or certify provenance or manipulation. A current satellite view cannot prove that an image was taken at a particular place or time.
nodes.norm_label: god's eye view does not authenticate an image

nodes.label: Recommended Hackathon MVP for Image Verification
nodes.community_name: IFM Video Need: Authenticate Images for Journalists
nodes.description: The memo recommends demonstrating one verifiable photo case, optionally a video frame, with context, available clues and their limits, traceable sources, and a cautious conclusion with justified confidence and next steps.
nodes.norm_label: recommended hackathon mvp for image verification
nodes.rationale: The memo explicitly derives this recommendation from the video and the general scoring standard, and says it is not an official IFM requirement.

nodes.label: Laverta by Urbix: Brand Identity
nodes.community_name: IFM Video Need: Authenticate Images for Journalists
nodes.description: The team selected Laverta to replace Hamarino. Proposed signature: “La correction doit suivre la rumeur.” Proposed promise: detect earlier, verify faster, correct further.

nodes.label: IFM Video Need: Authenticate Images for Journalists
nodes.community_name: IFM Video Need: Authenticate Images for Journalists
nodes.description: The video describes a need for journalists in Madagascar to verify information professionally using explainable evidence and verifiable sources, with photos and videos as the initial priority. Multilingual access, regional coverage and source directories are additional expectations; the memo notes that its transcript is a working transcription.
nodes.norm_label: ifm video need: authenticate images for journalists

nodes.label: Prebunking Before High-Risk Periods
nodes.description: A separate preventive measure proposes warning messages before periods such as cyclone season, elections or epidemics so people learn to check before sharing.

nodes.label: Laverta Target Functional Scope
nodes.description: Team-defined target scope, not implemented-state reporting: multilingual and multichannel intake; assistive OCR, transcription, language and claim extraction, duplicate suggestions and explainable priority; distinct reverse-image/video/text search and official-source modules; journalist case queue; invited organization responses; correction distribution; early warning and prebunking; impact measures, administration and security.

nodes.label: Aspirational Impact Targets
nodes.description: The PDF labels the proposed impact as an objective: reduce time from first report to correction from several days to hours, or seconds for a previously checked rumor, and extend correction reach from media readers to reporters, their groups and relay networks. These are targets, not measured results.

nodes.label: Faster Verification Lever
nodes.description: The PDF proposes rapid answers for rumors already checked, AI-assisted duplicate grouping, summaries and verification plans, and direct contact with relevant organizations. These are strategy proposals, not measured capabilities.

nodes.label: Early Rumor Detection Lever
nodes.description: The PDF proposes rapid-volume alerts (illustrated by 15 reports in one hour), a region-and-sector rumor map, and monitoring public pages through Meta's official API so journalists can respond early.

nodes.label: Web README Current Prototype State
nodes.description: The Next.js web prototype inherited from Hamarino has a public landing page, email authentication with Better Auth and PostgreSQL, and an image-verification area. The broader Laverta reporting and correction workflow is not fully developed.

nodes.label: README Prototype and Roadmap Boundary
nodes.description: The README describes the current Hamarino-derived prototype as a Laverta landing page, Better Auth/PostgreSQL login and Gemini image-context analysis. LV reports and tracking, journalist cases, verdicts, correction delivery, messaging, maps and statistics are roadmap items; the first priority is a real report-to-correction loop.

nodes.label: Current Laverta Prototype State
nodes.description: The rebranded Hamarino prototype has a Laverta landing page, Better Auth with PostgreSQL, a protected image-checking space, and server-side Gemini image analysis with Google Search and available citations. The simulation without a key must remain clearly labeled. Laverta reports, LV tracking, editorial cases, verdicts, correction delivery, and other roadmap functions are not implemented.

nodes.label: Web Prototype Data and Roadmap Boundary
nodes.community_name: Claude Code Product and Editorial Constraints
nodes.description: PostgreSQL currently stores account and session data only. Before reports or media are added, define retention, anonymization, access and deletion; do not present roadmap integrations as available before implementation.
nodes.norm_label: web prototype data and roadmap boundary

nodes.label: Claude Code Product and Editorial Constraints
nodes.community_name: Claude Code Product and Editorial Constraints
nodes.description: Verify implementation before claiming a feature is complete. AI assists with triage and preparation; journalists select statuses and approve corrections. Keep reporters masked by default, avoid absolute anonymity claims, and resolve access, retention, deletion and audit requirements before opening reports publicly. Labels and mockups must distinguish proposals and concepts from real verification.
nodes.norm_label: claude code product and editorial constraints

nodes.label: Laverta End-to-End Reporting and Correction Workflow
nodes.community_name: Laverta End-to-End Reporting and Correction Workflow
nodes.description: A person submits a claim or media with consent and receives a tracking identifier; the system proposes language, claim, theme, duplicates and research leads; a journalist reviews sources, contacts an organization if needed, chooses and justifies the verdict, approves a correction, and sends it through authorized channels.
nodes.norm_label: laverta end-to-end reporting and correction workflow

nodes.label: Reporter, Journalist, and Organization Workflow
nodes.community_name: Laverta End-to-End Reporting and Correction Workflow
nodes.description: Reporters submit, review, consent, track by code and may receive a correction. Journalists review the queue and sources, choose a justified verdict, approve correction and select channels. Organizations receive invited access only to forwarded anonymized cases. Case statuses are distinct from verdicts; lack of a source is not a false verdict.

nodes.label: Laverta Visual and Interface System
nodes.description: Ink, paper, warm white, forest and deep green, soft citron and terracotta form the palette; Geist Sans and Geist Serif serve operational and editorial text. Verdicts are written explicitly and never encoded by color alone. Motion is brief and accessible, with reduced-motion, keyboard and screen-reader support.

nodes.label: God's Eye View Geospatial Tool and Coverage Limits
nodes.community_name: God's Eye View Geospatial Tool and Coverage Limits
nodes.description: The analyzed project is a Vue, Pinia, CesiumJS and Vite globe showing public geospatial feeds and maps. Data sources have separate conditions and coverage; this local copy had no source dedicated to Madagascar or Antananarivo, and missing map points do not prove an event did not occur.
